key_insight: A large fraction of token-to-token attention scores in spatiotemporal transformers are consistently negligible and often repeat across queries, so skipping those computations via a calibrated sparse attention mask speeds up text-to-video diffusion models with minimal quality loss.
problem_solved: Slow inference and high compute cost of transformer-based spatiotemporal attention in text-to-video diffusion models that bottleneck practical generation throughput and scalability.
method: Analyze attention score statistics to identify token-to-token connections that are consistently low-impact and exhibit repeating patterns across queries.
Construct a calibrated sparse attention mechanism that skips computation for those negligible connections while adjusting (calibrating) remaining weights to preserve output fidelity.
Integrate the sparse attention into the diffusion-based text-to-video transformer backbone to reduce runtime and memory without significant degradation in generated video quality.
impact: Substantially reduces inference time and compute for text-to-video generation, lowering cost and enabling faster iteration, higher throughput, or support for longer/higher-resolution videos in research and production settings.
visual_elements: Attention heatmap vs. sparse mask: show full dense attention heatmap alongside the sparse mask highlighting pruned (skipped) connections.
Before/after pipeline diagram: model inference flow with dense attention (slow, high compute) vs. calibrated sparse attention (faster, lower compute) and annotated speedup/memory savings.
Bar chart: quantitative tradeoff—runtime and GPU memory vs. video quality (e.g., FID or perceptual score) demonstrating minimal quality loss for large speed gains.
Token graph schematic: spatiotemporal tokens with edges colored/removed to illustrate recurring negligible connections and the pruning rationale.
paper_title: Accelerating Text-to-Video Generation with Calibrated Sparse Attention
paper_authors: Shai Yehezkel, Shahar Yadin, Noam Elata, Yaron Ostrovsky-Berman, Bahjat Kawar
